1503866964711997440 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 14 🔁 1
This has apparently become a hot take: status interactions matter, the winning move is not "ignore status." Doing so is blinding yourself to what your senses are informing you about the world. There are status interactions going on in everything we do. You can't opt out.
↓
1503866967987724288 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 6
That said, there's a reason that ignoring status interactions can sometimes be a superpower, it's the same reason that self-deception can make you a better liar: two separate narratives are harder to manage than one.
↓
1503866971816931331 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 8 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
It's hard for most folx to convincingly tell a bald faced lie, that is, telling a lie they know to be a lie. This is a cognitively costly process that requires you keep both the truth and the lie in mind at once. It's easier to rewrite your story so the lie is just a truth.
↓
1503866976049205249 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 6
In the same way, status has two parts: how you really feel about yourself and your relationship to who you're speaking with, and the separately, there is the status you're trying to play during the interaction.
↓
1503866978498658305 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 5
Keeping track of both of these things is hard, but so is inflicting the status on yourself, enter: just ignore status. By Just Ignoring Status, you shunt the process off onto S1. If your intuitions aren't entirely bad, this comes off better than brute forcing it with S2.
↓
1503866980843286528 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 5
However, your S1 isn't perfectly trained, if you totally abandon participation in the process you're left at the whims of all those biases. This is the danger with Just Ignoring Status. You can't just not participate.
↓
1503866982718148609 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 6
Taking control of the process also means you're responsible for the process in a way few people would like to admit, because doing so makes interactions more costly and creates additional expectations. However, all this said, taking control of the process gives better results.
↓
1503866986043957249 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 6
It takes work to train the skill of navigating status consciously, just like it takes skill to learn to lie convincingly (acting). If you train this skill, it's kind of a superpower, and will allow you to understand and navigate social interactions with ease.
↓
1503866989009580033 [2022-03-15] @slimepriestess 💜 10
You just need to be willing to get through the awkward phase of learning how to see and engage with status games without letting your social anxieties push you into uncomfortable and adversarial mindsets. Status games don't have to be hostile, sometimes they're just fun.

===

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand centers on Romeo Stevens' 2022 tweet about the brain being 'not type safe'—the idea that lying to others and lying to yourself are the same cognitive motion. The discourse evolves from a simple observation into a multi-year exploration of its implications across domains: self-deception, status games, forgiveness, encouragement, and truth-seeking. The arc is primarily *constructive*—people riff on and apply the concept rather than challenging it. The boundary object is the 'type safety' metaphor itself, which becomes a shared vocabulary for discussing how internal and external behaviors leak into each other. The strand shows medium evolution (new applications emerge but the core idea remains stable) and high cohesion (recurring participants like Tasshin, Romeo, and others keep returning to refine it).

essential_tweets.annotation: The Artifact: Romeo's original 'brain is not type safe' formulation, establishing the core metaphor
Expansion into status games: Slimepriestess applies the concept to self-deception as a cognitive cost-saving mechanism
Bidirectional leak: Tasshin connects the concept to judgment—freeing yourself from judging others frees you from self-judgment
Ill will variant: Romeo extends the pattern to cultivating hostility toward others as type-unsafe with self-hostility
Canonical synthesis: Tasshin includes it in his 'Threadapalooza' summary of recurring ideas in the community
Formal notation: Tasshin reformulates the idea as 'functions called on self leak to other, functions called on world leak to self'
Empirical validation: Research showing BS artists fall for BS—external evidence supporting the type-unsafety thesis
Practical application: Mae describes learning to tell the truth as 'life-changing,' showing real-world utility
Forgiveness extension: Tasshin applies the concept positively—forgiving others makes self-forgiveness possible
Maximalist synthesis: Theralkia frames lying as 'the worst thing' because it cements false self-image and unconsciousness
